On Oct. 28, Google's parent company Alphabet reported that its search queries were growing at their fastest annual rate in five years, with total Q3 revenues nearing $127.6 billion, up 25% year-on-year.

However, a deeper analysis reveals a more troubling trend: more people are searching, but Google's AI-driven search experiences aren't yet generating ad revenue at the same rate as conventional search. Revenue from "Search & other" increased 12% to $63.35 billion, with chief business officer Philipp Schindler acknowledging that AI Mode's comparatively limited monetization had contributed to the slowdown.

Alphabet shares fell approximately 12.6% on Oct. 29, erasing close to $500 billion in market value. Sundar Pichai told analysts that AI Mode queries are, on average, three times longer than traditional searches, while approximately one in five involves voice, images or documents.

Executives hinted that Google is expanding advertising within AI Mode internationally and introducing multi-turn advertisements in the U.S. Meanwhile, Google Network revenues rose a modest 1.4%, while traffic acquisition costs hit $16.4 billion.

Three Claude models picked from the same 20 Shopify products 1,980 times and never agreed on the top product. Each search was run once through Shop MCP, the connection Shopify opened to AI agents on Oct. 13, and the models were Claude Haiku 4.5, Sonnet 5 and Opus 5.

On the six product searches, the three models' most-picked product matched in none. Each model was consistent with itself: Sonnet's most-picked product took 94% of its picks on average, Opus's 89%, and Haiku's 67%.

Haiku and Sonnet picked the product with the most reviews, including a water bottle listed at 5.0 stars from 447,221 reviews, about 68 times the count nobl's product page shows. In 222 of its 300 picks, Opus 5 called its choice "safe" or "safest".

Moving the catalog's top product from first to last made the models almost stop picking it on some searches, and in 480 reasons, not one mentioned where a product sat in the list. When the request added "under $25, for oily skin", the models picked a sunscreen under $25 in 298 of 300 picks.

Google's Ads Decoded podcast on October 28 published a 25-minute episode in which Shivani Mohan, Search Vice President of Data Science and User Experience Research at Google, said that query length "has increased 3x" and that "one in every six searches is multimodal."

Host Ginny Marvin, Google's Ads Product Liaison, said ads in AI Mode and AI Overviews are "matched to both the query and the content of the AI response," and pointed retailers to six optional product data fields, Merchant Center's new conversational attributes.

Neither figure came with a market, a time period or a baseline. Google's May 19 report put the average AI Mode query at three times the length of a traditional search query and said more than one in six AI Mode searches in the United States were multimodal. Neither speaker said AI Mode or the United States when giving the numbers.

Mohan said queries are "moving up the funnel," and Marvin told advertisers to recalibrate search "outside of last click action." The episode offered no performance data for ads in either AI surface: no click-through rates, no conversion rates and no cost comparison with ads on the standard results page.

Nearly a quarter of U.S. consumers have bought a product based on an AI recommendation. Of those, nearly half (46%) have returned an item in the past year, according to a Blue Yonder survey. The most common reasons were that it was different than described (36%) or an incorrect size or fit (23%).

While incorrect size or fit is the most common factor leading to U.S. returns in general (42%), the most frequently cited problem with AI-recommended products is that the item doesn't live up to its description.

"That's not really an AI problem. It's a data problem," Blue Yonder CEO Duncan Angove said. "An AI assistant is only as good as the product information it can find, and most product data was written for a search bar, not for a machine suggesting products for someone."

Of the 2,000 U.S. shoppers surveyed, 43% of Gen Z bought a product based on an AI recommendation, compared to 36% of millennials, 19% of Gen X and 9% of baby boomers. Over half (51%) said they have chosen one retailer over another purely because of a better returns policy.

In U.S. traffic, a visit from a ChatGPT ad brought in $0.89 in revenue, against $2.45 for a visit from a paid Google search ad, according to a working paper by Maximilian Kaiser and Christian Schulze. Its paid-ad figures come from 102 advertiser sites with full sales tracking.

ChatGPT ad visits converted at 0.37 percent versus 1.17 percent with paid search. Among the 87 advertisers who purchased both, 84 had lower earnings per ChatGPT ad visit; 73 had zero sales from their ChatGPT ads, while the remaining 14 generated all 570 ChatGPT ad purchases.

At paid search's rate of return, the authors value a ChatGPT ad click at about $0.26 (a resampled range of $0.05 to $0.57). The largest publicly known account paid $1.72 per click, more than six times the parity price.

Organic ChatGPT referrals fell an estimated 6%–8% after ads arrived. The paper's data ends Aug. 22; OpenAI has since expanded ChatGPT Ads to 89 countries and says more than 100,000 advertisers have run campaigns.
The Trade Desk is connecting Ask Koa, its conversational agentic platform, with adtech firm Dstillery’s agentic platform, DS-1, to help ad buyers create custom audiences in minutes rather than days.

Roku Nov. 4 announced the beta launch of Roku Outcomes, an AI-driven advertising platform that allows marketers to optimize streaming TV campaigns for specific actions.

Visa has launched the Visa Agentic Commerce Benchmark, finding that 22 AI models passed 57.2% of realistic shopping tests overall. “As agentic commerce meets advertising, the definition of an impression is critical as well as the reporting and measurement,” said independent ad tech consultant Jonathan D’Sousa-Rauto. Requests carry across the Amazon Shopping app, the site and Alexa-enabled devices, and through Shop Direct the agent can also buy from stores beyond Amazon.

blocks.x: Google released version 0.0.6 of its open-source Google Ads MCP server on November 2, 2026, adding the first tools in the project's public history that can change a Google Ads account. The four write tools — create_asset, upload_video_asset, manage_labels and manage_label_associations — create assets, upload videos to YouTube and manage labels, each gated behind a two-step dry run and checksum. Recent reports found that the artificial intelligence-powered ad tools posted discount offers to customers even with promotions turned off.

Ads in which fake doctors made with artificial intelligence (AI) explain a cosmetic's effects and recommend using it become an explicit legal target for prohibition from the end of this month. Article 13, Paragraph 1, Item 4 of the revised Cosmetics Act, which takes effect on the 27th, bans ads that risk misleading consumers into thinking that AI-generated virtual experts such as doctors, pharmacists or university professors recommend or endorse a cosmetic.

Using AI technology to make ads is not itself banned. The test is whether a virtual expert who is hard to tell apart from a real one risks leading consumers to mistake the ad for an expert's recommendation or endorsement.

According to a Korea Consumer Agency survey, 420 unfair ads misusing AI were caught in YouTube ads from October last year to June this year, and 72 of them (17.1%) were cosmetics ads. Ads impersonating experts also reached 153.

The image generator "can implement three different weights of the stable diffusion model" - an inpainting model, SDXL and a fine-tuned model - with keyword prompts and negative prompts such as "NSFW," "text" and "logo."

Nothing has been granted or launched. The filing contains no performance data and never names the App Store, Apple Ads or App Store Connect, referring only to an "online software application store."

No major retail media player has taken as circumspect an approach to advertising revenue as Shopify, which holds the greatest supply of such first-party data outside of Amazon and Walmart. After data partnerships and addressable audience segments for other platforms, its next step is Campaign Autopilot, Samir Pradhan, Shopify VP of product for merchant marketing, told AdExchanger.

It's an agentic, AI-driven optimization product: merchants set the price they're willing to pay per sale, with controls such as a higher incentive for new customers or targeting by region or time of day. Partner platforms are Meta, Microsoft Advertising and Snapchat, with X in the pipeline, plus email marketing and ads on Shop. SEO optimization was added in the past few weeks.

Pradhan called it a “risk-free ad product”: other platforms charge per impression and/or for clicks, but with Autopilot “Shopify takes that media risk” and the merchant only pays per sale. Campaigns can be capped or a channel avoided, and “preserving that merchant trust and then making them feel in control was a big part of the ethos of developing this product.”

WPP agency Ogilvy has inked a partnership with Creative Artists Agency (CAA) to generate AI ads featuring the actors, athletes and high-profile creators on CAA’s roster. “We are witnessing the ‘NIL moment’ between advertising and entertainment,” said Carol Reed, global chief innovation officer at Ogilvy. Brooklyn Nine-Nine star Terry Crews is among the actors who have opted in, and pilots “should be going live towards the end of the year.”

The solution, called Echo, gives Ogilvy access to material kept in “The Vault,” an in-house digital scanning facility built for CAA by Veritone four years ago that uses 204 cameras to capture an actor, athlete or creator’s voice, body language, facial expressions and walk. Staffers can pull it into WPP Open for storyboarding, mock-ups or final creative assets, with cost-per-asset expected to fall by 65-75%.

CAA clients own their digital likenesses and choose which businesses and markets they appear for. “Talent always gets to see everything and approve everything at the end,” said Reed. AI ad materials will carry a watermark marking them as AI-generated and approved by the star.

Consumers remain cool on the idea: nearly half (49%) of Britons view AI-generated actors in ads negatively, according to YouGov. Reed said the system is an extension of Ogilvy’s “palette” and that “there is a human craft and a human behind it.”

Until then, that 13-page guidance maps seven existing MRC standards and guidelines onto nine AI principles in 58 appendix entries — requirements auditors already apply, from disclosure of model error rates to feature importance and model cards for auctions.

Reddit announced a partnership with predictive inference company Qloo (pronounced “clue”) on Tuesday, giving it access to over 10 years of Qloo’s proprietary data to serve more relevant ads. Qloo’s catalogue tracks correlations between interests, or “entities,” like restaurants and musical artists, based on shared attributes drawn from TasteDive reviews, Wikidata metadata and licensed third-party data.

Finding shared attributes that aren’t obvious at first glance is why Reddit partnered with Qloo, said Virgilio Pigliucci, Reddit’s senior director of engineering. People shopping for an espresso machine often also want a table for it, so Reddit might serve an ad for a tall desk on a coffeemaker thread.

Optimizing a new advertiser’s campaign used to take days or weeks of engagement data. Now Reddit can “optimize against the signals” from Qloo, and the model draws correlations without knowing a user’s search query, browsing history or subreddit, so advertisers see results “right away.”

Local life platform Daangn has begun automating ad operations with artificial intelligence (AI). After introducing a feature that lets advertisers analyze ad performance from outside AI services such as ChatGPT and Claude, it has opened an application programming interface (API) that also lets them register and edit ads.

According to the industry on the 9th, Daangn is upgrading the ‘Ad Model Context Protocol (MCP)’ it launched for advertisers in September. MCP is a technology that helps AI models and agents connect to external systems to look up data or carry out tasks.

With Daangn’s ad MCP, advertisers can connect their Daangn ad account to the AI they normally use and check ad status and performance in natural language. Ask “Summarize my ad performance for the last 7 days,” and the AI pulls the data from the ad account and organizes it. Advertisers can look up and compare ad accounts and balances, running ads and performance by period.

Last month Daangn also released a beta of its ad Open API, which lets external systems call Daangn’s ad functions directly. From their own ad management tools or internal dashboards, advertisers can look up, register or edit campaigns, ad groups and ad creatives.

The change comes because many of Daangn’s main advertisers are small business owners with little experience running ads. The calculation is that if they can lift ad performance simply by asking the AI they already use, they will place more ads on Daangn.

Kakao will also start a closed beta test next month of ‘AI Crew,’ an AI agent that supports advertisers in buying and running ads. With AI Crew, advertisers enter their business goals into a conversational interface and the AI suggests suitable ad products and operating strategies.
United says it won’t let personal AI assistants book tickets on the airline, citing both privacy and regulatory concerns.

The company says it hasn’t yet seen many people try to use AI agents to book their flights, The Wall Street Journal reports, in line with observations from other businesses like Doordash. But United is concerned that agents could expose customers’ information or make purchases they didn’t intend, and potentially skirt federal rules about the kind of information airlines need to share with customers — like having them attest that their bags don’t have explosives.

While agents can still show users United flights, they won’t be able to actually complete the transaction on their behalf. The decision, and others like it, could limit the potential usefulness of newer personal AI assistants like Meta’s Muse and OpenAI’s Dots. “To be honest, I don’t want to create another middleman,” United CEO Scott Kirby said at an event on Tuesday, according to the Journal.

Across sectors, businesses are grappling with whether to let AI agents transact on their sites, and United is not alone in blocking access for unauthorized agents. eBay appeared to block agents from browsing the site, and several major banks have also placed restrictions on them. United suggests it could reconsider its decision based on future advancements. “As third-party AI agents advance, we see the opportunities they present. However, at the same time, allowing them to interact directly with a United account or booking could involve sensitive actions, and we want to make sure we have established protections for travelers first.”

blocks.x: The European Commission's guidelines on the transparency obligations in Article 50 of the AI Act were published in the Official Journal of the European Union under the reference C/2026/6005. A company established outside the EU that uses an AI system to generate a deep fake of a celebrity for an advertisement displayed in the Union is, according to the guidelines, a deployer within the scope of the AI Act.

AI-made celebrity endorsements, synthetic influencers testing products and product images that misrepresent the real item all count as deep fakes that need a visible label. A company that merely commissions an agency, without control over how it uses AI, is not a deployer. Ad copy and product descriptions stay outside the text rule unless they make health, consumer safety or sustainability claims.

Deployers "cannot rely on the machine-readable marking embedded in the content by the provider." Fines for breaching Article 50 reach EUR 15,000,000 or 3% of total worldwide annual turnover, whichever is higher. Generative systems placed on the market before August 2, 2026 have until December 2, 2026 to meet the marking duty.

Shoppers using AI chatbots to research products or find places to buy items could be directed to imposters and other risky websites, a new study found. IP protection firm Podqi prompted ChatGPT, Gemini, and Perplexity with shopping-related questions involving 151 brands, such as “Where can I find [brand] online?”

Over the course of 6,795 answers, all three AI engines cited and showed shoppers risky sites, defined as fake websites impersonating real retailers or selling knockoffs, reregistered old brand domains, or dead sites. Gemini showed risky sites in 4 percent of answers, ChatGPT in 8 percent, and Perplexity performed the worst at 15 percent. Smaller brands appear especially at risk.

In one conversation, Perplexity named the wrong page as Stüssy’s official website and called it “the best starting point for guaranteed authentic items.” “It is always best to verify the source of that before entering personal information or credit card information,” says Podqi CEO and cofounder Trevor West.
